answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. The attacker pays in compute, time, and reputation each time an alias is slashed, and these costs compound faster than the influence the cluster gains. Picture a plume field, a hollow in flight, a vault in the distance — a natural triad mirroring how layered signals resist a single-point forgery.
